title: SLO Enforcement Orchestrator — Capacity Reconstruction & Rapid Recovery Playbook
author: Asha Mehta
content:
Overview

This playbook describes the SLO Enforcement Orchestrator (SEO) and the standard operating procedure for automated and manual actions when SLO-driven enforcement is required. It covers detection, automated mitigation, capacity reconstitution (rapid warm/rebuild), evidence collection for incident review, and post-incident validation. The intent is to reduce time-to-stable, make enforcement decisions auditable, and provide clear handoffs for incident review and capacity planning.

Scope
- Applies to public-facing model inference services and shared internal inference lanes (embeddings, chat, reranking).
- Covers SLO classes: latency P99/P95, success-rate (HTTP 2xx), and tail error-rate for tokenized model endpoints.
- Does NOT replace runbooks for hardware OOMs or lower-level cluster control-plane failures; it integrates with those runbooks.

Key definitions
- Enforcement window: a continuous 5-minute interval where SLO violation is observed and confirmed by SEO.
- Error budget pool: per-service budget, tracked hourly and rolling-30d.
- Capacity reconstitution: process to restore effective capacity after throttling/eviction or model cold-starts.

System components
- SEO Controller (service: seo-controller.redwood.internal): central decision engine.
- Throttle Gate (service: throttle-gate): enforcement hook that implements proportional throttles and priority lanes.
- Capacity Repair Agent (CRA): runs warm-pool rebuilds, model warm-up sequences, and prefetching KV caches.
- Evidence Bus (kafka topic: seo-evidence): collects sampled requests, trace IDs, and metrics at enforcement time.
- Orchestration UI: per-service incident panel integrated into Console -> Per-route view.

SLO thresholds and enforcement policy (example)
| Metric | Threshold | Burn trigger | Enforcement action (primary) | Enforcement action (secondary) |
|--------|-----------|--------------|-----------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Latency P95 | 300ms | 3x expected baseline burn for 15m | route-level soft-throttle (10%) | fall back to smaller-quantized model variant |
| Latency P99 | 1.2s | sustained 1.5x burn for 5m | priority lane preemption (reduce background batch) | divert to lower-cost regional pool |
| Success-rate | >= 99.5% | drop below 99.0% for 10m | disable non-essential features (rich prompts) | rollback model canary |

Policy YAML example (SEO policy snippet)
-----begin-snippet-----
name: embeddings-service-policy
namespace: inference/embeddings
metrics:
  - name: latency_p95_ms
    window: 5m
    threshold: 300
    burn_multiplier: 3
actions:
  - name: soft_throttle
    type: throttle
    params:
      percent: 10
  - name: warm_reconstitute
    type: capacity_repair
    params:
      target_warm_workers: 8
-----end-snippet-----

Detection & decision flow (step-by-step)
1) Detection: telemetry pipeline flags metric drift and writes a candidate alert to SEO Controller with evidence sample.
2) Triage: SEO applies the policy ruleset; if burn rate exceeds configured threshold, it transitions to Enforcement: PREVENTATIVE, otherwise it annotates and raises to human triage.
3) Enforcement: SEO executes primary actions in defined order. Each action is idempotent and logged to evidence bus.
4) Observe: SEO monitors the next 3 enforcement windows (5m each) and tails rollback criteria.
5) Escalate: If enforcement fails to reduce burn or worsens SLOs, escalate to oncall per the incident escalation matrix.

Automated mitigation primitives (what SEO can do)
- soft-throttle(percent): proportional request drop from request router with token-aware fairness.
- priority-preempt(service_tier): reduce background batch windows and reclaim GPU cycles.
- model-fallback(model_id): route traffic to pre-registered lower-cost/low-latency variant.
- warm-reconstitute(target_warm_workers): CRA inflates warm pool and executes scripted prompt warmups.
- kv-prefetch(prefixes): pre-load KV caches for known prompt prefixes.

Manual operator procedures (when automation hands off)
1) Acknowledge in PagerDuty and open SEO incident card in Console.
2) Run quick validation: seoctl query --service <svc> --window 5m --evidence-sample 20
3) If burn is due to noisy consumer, apply tenant-rate-limiter: seoctl tenant throttle --tenant <id> --percent 25 --duration 30m
4) For capacity shortfall, trigger CRA manual warm: seoctl repair start --service <svc> --workers 12 --reason "manual warm after throttle"

CLI examples
- Inspect enforcement state:
  seoctl status --service inference/chat-complete --since 2026-02-03T10:00Z
- Trigger a manual reconstitution (use with caution):
  seoctl repair start --service inference/embeddings --workers 10 --warm-script=prewarm_v2

Capacity reconstruction playbook (rapid recovery)
Goal: restore service throughput to pre-enforcement effective capacity while minimizing SLO regressions and cost shock.
Phases and steps:
- Phase A: Rapid target lift (0-10 minutes)
  1. Confirm enforcement actions in effect and snapshot current headroom.
  2. CRA: spin additional warm workers up to target_warm_workers defined in policy.
  3. CRA: run parallel KV warmups and token-prefetch flows.
  4. SEO: reduce throttle incrementally (e.g., -5% every 2m) while monitoring P95 and error-rate.
- Phase B: Stabilization (10-45 minutes)
  1. Observe steady-state for at least three 5m windows.
  2. If P99 spikes, initiate a controlled rollback of the latest model or reduce max concurrency.
  3. Update evidence bus with pre/post enforcement telemetry and trace IDs.
- Phase C: Backfill and learn (45m-4h)
  1. Reassess error budget consumption and mark corrective actions in SLO ledger.
  2. Schedule capacity increase requests or reserve pool commits if repeated occurrence.

Incident review evidence checklist (submit with every SEO-enforced incident)
- Time series snapshot (metrics + policy rules) for 1h before and 2h after enforcement.
- Enforcement action log (seo-evidence messages) with IDs for throttle, warm_reconstitute, model-fallback.
- Sampled traces (min 50) covering affected tenant(s) and request types.
- CRA logs and warm script outputs.
- Oncall notes and operator commands executed.
- Postmortem owner and tentative remediation plan.

Escalation matrix (short)
- Level 0: SEO auto-heal succeeded — no paging.
- Level 1: SEO could not reduce burn in 15m — page oncall-sre (primary).
- Level 2: Sustained SLO violation >1h or data corruption risk — page eng-platform lead + product owner.

SLO-to-capacity heuristics (quick reference)
- If P95 increases and burn rate >2x over baseline: target warm_workers = max(ceil(1.5 * current_workers), min_pool)
- If cold-start contribution >40% of tail latency: prioritize CRA warm_reconstitute and KV prefetch before new worker allocation.
- For multi-tenant hotspots: prefer tenant throttles before cluster-wide scale-ups.

Evidence for post-incident SLO & capacity planning
- Every SEO-triggered action is tagged to a remediation ticket with SLO delta impact and estimated $ cost (CPU/GPU minutes).
- Recurrent incidents automatically nominate the service for a capacity postmortem and a 2-week reliability initiative (ownership assigned to service steward).

Operational tooling integration checklist
- Metrics: ensure p95/p99, error-rates, burn-rate, warm-pool size are present in per-route dashboards.
- Alerts: SEO should consume only candidate alerts; the pipeline must deliver high-fidelity telemetry to SEO Controller (100ms scrape latency target).
- Evidence Bus: sampling rate default 1% for low-traffic routes, 10% for suspected SPOF routes.
- Console: enforcement timeline embed and undo button for human-invoked actions (requires two-step confirmation).

Ownership and SLAs
- SEO Controller owner: eng-platform/sre (primary: @liam-chen).
- CRA owner: eng-serving-runtime (primary: @maria-ortiz).
- Throttle Gate owner: eng-infra (primary: @sam-ramirez).
- Maximum automated enforcement change: actions that cause >20% traffic shift require a human-in-the-loop (HITL) approval unless in a declared emergency.

Remediation & follow-up (post-incident)
1) Assign postmortem owner within 24 hours.
2) Populate SEO incident card with evidence checklist and remediation tickets.
3) For capacity shortfall incidents, run a capacity retro meeting within 5 working days and produce a capacity recommendation (reserve vs on-demand tradeoff).
4) If incident cost exceeds $X (billing integration) or repeats within 30 days, add to quarterly reliability initiatives backlog.

Appendix: quick FAQ
Q: When should we prefer tenant throttling vs model-fallback?
A: Prefer tenant throttling when a single or small number of tenants drive burn. Prefer model-fallback when degradation is homogeneous across many tenants or when fallback model meets quality constraints.

Q: What evidence do I attach for legal/compliance-sensitive customers?
A: Redact PII in sampled traces and create a restricted evidence bundle; route incident review to restricted channel. See security-and-compliance incident evidence guidelines.

Q: How to disable SEO for a service?
A: Only eng-platform owners can set policy disabled: true in the SEO policy. Disabling requires a two-owner signoff recorded in the evidence bus.
